questions.question: The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act 2003 set a target to limit India’s fiscal deficit up to ________ of the GDP by 2021.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__ **3%.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Targets and fiscal indicators under FRBM Act 2003**:-

 
 
• **The government is required to limit the fiscal deficit to 3% of the GDP by March 31, 2021.**
 
• The government is required** to limit the debt of the central government to 40% of the GDP by the year 2024-25.**
 
 
 
• ​The** FRBM rules mandate four fiscal indicators** to be projected in the medium-term fiscal policy statement.
 
• These are:
 
 
• **Revenue deficit as a percentage of GDP.**
 
 
• The revenue deficit should be completely eliminated by March 31, 2009.
 
• The minimum annual reduction target was 0.5% of GDP.
 
 
 
• **Fiscal deficit as a percentage of GDP.**
 
 
• The fiscal deficit should be reduced to 3% of GDP by March 31, 2009.
 
• The minimum annual reduction target was 0.3% of GDP.
 
 
 
• **Tax revenue as a percentage of GDP.**
 
• Total outstanding liabilities as a percentage of GDP.
 
 
 
• The** FRBM Act set targets for fiscal deficit and revenue deficit.​**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act (FRBM Act), 2003**,

 
 
• **Establishes financial discipline** to reduce the fiscal deficit.
 
• The FRBM Bill was** introduced by the then finance minister, Yashwant Sinha, in 2000.**
 
• The Bill, approved by the Union Cabinet in 2003, **became effective on July 5, 2004.**
 
• The FRBM Act** aims to introduce transparency in India's fiscal management systems.**
 
• The FRBM Act** aimed to introduce a more equitable distribution** of India's debt over the years.
 
• It is an **Act to provide:**
 
 
• the** responsibility of the Central Government to ensure inter-generational equity** in fiscal management.
 
• **long-term macroeconomic stability **by removing fiscal impediments in the effective conduct of monetary policy.
 
• **prudential debt management** is consistent with fiscal sustainability.
 
• **limits on the Central Government borrowings and debt.**
 
• greater transparency in fiscal operations of the Central Government.​

questions.question: While trying to promote growth by tax cuts as the fiscal policy, which type of policy is the government trying to follow?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Expansionary.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** expansionary policy** aims to stimulate the economy by** boosting demand through monetary and fiscal stimulus.**
 
• Expansionary policy is intended to **prevent or moderate economic downturns and recessions.**
 
• ​The Expansionary fiscal policy involves **reducing taxes or increasing government **spending to increase aggregate demand and production output.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Contractionary policy:**

 
 
• Contractionary policy is a monetary measure referring either** to a reduction in government spending or a reduction in the rate of monetary expansion** by a central bank.
 
• Contractionary policy is the** opposite of expansionary policy.**
 
• It is undertaken to combat rising inflation or other economic distortions created by central banks or government interventions. 
 
 
 
• **Easy money:**
 
 
• **Easy money **is a way for the central bank to build more cash within the economic system.
 
• Easy money occurs when a central bank wants to make money flow between banks more easily.
 
• When banks have access to more money, interest rates charged to customers go down because banks have more money than needed to invest.
 
 
 
• **Tight money:**
 
 
• Tight money usually restrict the money supply and reduces the number of money banks have to lend.
 
• It can also be the result of an increased demand to hold money when the quantity of money remains unchanged.

questions.question: Which ITNS (Income Tax New Series) challan is used by Indian taxpayers to deposit the tax collected at source?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**ITNS 281**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **TDS and TCS **are deposited using **Challan No. ITNS 281** by both corporate and non-corporate entities.
 
• TDS (Tax Deducted at Source) is a government-instituted mechanism in which a person (deductor) deducts tax at a specified percentage from an amount payable to the payee (deductee) before making a payment of a specified nature (such as salary, rent, etc.) and deposits it with the Income Tax Department.
 
• TCS or Tax Collected at Source, is the tax that the seller collects from the buyer at the time of the sale of certain items.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Income Tax Department's Challan ITNS 284 **is used to pay Income Tax on Corporations (Corporation Tax) and Income Tax on Other than Corporations.
 
• **The Income Tax Department's Challan ITNS 283** is used to pay the Banking Cash Transaction Tax and Fringe Benefits Tax.
 
• To deposit gift tax, estate duty, spending tax, and other miscellaneous taxes, **ITNS 282 form is used.**

questions.question: Which was the only sector in the Indian economy that showed an increased GVA (Gross Value Added) of 3.4% in the first quarter of 2020?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Agriculture**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Agriculture **was the only sector in the Indian economy that showed an increased GVA (Gross Value Added) of 3.4% in the first quarter of 2020.
 
• Agriculture is set to cushion the shock of the COVID-19 pandemic on the Indian economy in 2020- 21 with a growth **of 3.4 per cent** resulting in an increase in its share in GDP to** 19.9 per cent in 2020-21** from **17.8 per cent in 2019-20.**
 
• The services sector accounts for** 53.89% of total India's GVA of 179.15 lakh crore Indian rupees.**
 
• With** GVA of Rs. 46.44 lakh crore,** the Industry sector **contributes 25.92%.**
 
• While Agriculture and** allied sector share 20.19%.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• Gross value added (GVA) is defined as output (at basic prices) minus intermediate consumption (at purchaser prices)
 
• It is the balancing item of the national accounts production account. GVA can be broken down by industry and institutional sector.
 
• Gross value added (GVA) is an economic productivity metric that measures the contribution of a corporate subsidiary, company, or municipality to an economy, producer, sector, or region
 
• Gross value added measures profits and wages of London-based businesses and London's employees.
 
 
• GVA= GDP + subsidies on products – taxes on products.

__**Taxes:**__ Tax is a compulsory payment by the citizens to the government to meet the expenditure. There are mainly two types of taxes.

__
 
• **Direct Tax:__ **is a tax paid directly to the government by the persons on whom it is imposed. Example** Income Tax, Land Tax, Property Tax, Corporation Tax, and Profession Tax.**
 
• __**Indirect Tax:**__ is levied on goods or services rather than individuals and is ultimately paid by consumers in the form of a higher price. Indirect taxation is a policy often used to generate tax revenue. Example **Excise Duty, Entertainment Tax, Sales Tax, Customs Duty, and Value Added Tax.**
 
• __**​GST (Goods and Services Tax):**__ is a comprehensive tax indirect tax on the manufacture, sale, and consumption of goods and services throughout India.
 __
 
• The motto of GST - **One Nation, One Tax, One Market**
 
• GST bill was passed by Rajya Sabha on **3rd August 2016.**
 
• GST bill was passed by Lok Sabha on **8th August 2016.**
 
• GST bill was signed by President on 8th **September 2016.**
 
• GST bill came into effect from 1st July 2017

questions.question: _______ tax is imposed on transactions that have a negative externality; for example, pollution.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pigovian**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pigouvian taxes **are taxes levied against **private individuals or businesses** for engaging in a specific **activity that causes a certain negative effect** on a commercial activity which affects other parties without this being reflected. Ex-** Causing environmental pollution**.
 
• Tax is **named after economist Arthur C. Pigou**, who mention or draw the** idea from his book The Economics of Welfare, 192**0.
 
• **Arun Jaitley** announced an increase in securities transaction taxes on **equity options from 0.017% to 0.05%**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****__Tax Definition__**

__
 
• A tax is a **legal fee or financial charge** levied by the government on an individual or an organization.

***​Type of Taxes__***

 
• **Direct tax -**Direct taxes are those in which the **point of impact and point of the incident will fall on the same entity**. A direct tax **cannot be transferred** by an individual to another person, example-**Income tax and corporate tax**.
 
• **Indirect tax-**Indirect tax is a type of tax where** the point of incident and impact does not fall on the same entity**. The burden of tax **can be transferred **by the taxpayer to another person, for example- **GST and Custom Duty**.

 
 

 **Taxes**
 **Meaning and Levied By**
 
 

 Income tax
 
 
Tax is applicable on the income earned by an individual or taxpayer.

 
Collected by the Central government.

 
 
 

 Corporate tax
 
 
The tax is applicable to the profits earned by companies from their businesses.

 
Collected by the Central Government

 
 
 

 GST
 
 
One Nation One Tax levied on goods and services used by the taxpayer.

 
Collected by the Central and State Government.

 
 
 

 Custom Duty
 
 
The tax is levied on the import and export of goods.

 
Collected by Central Government.
